name: Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge
description:
The Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge is a directional breaching charge that combines a shaped piezoelectric detonation wave with a tightly collimated acoustic frequency package tuned to cerebrospinal fluid resonance. When placed against a surface — wall, vehicle hull, or floor — the SSDC-4's primary piezoelectric initiator fires a shockwave through the intervening material at a frequency calculated to couple maximally with the subarachnoid space of anyone on the opposite side within a 2-meter radius. The result is traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage without structural breach of the barrier itself.

The charge was originally developed as a counter-hostage tool — a way to neutralize armed individuals behind cover without compromising the structural integrity needed for building clearance. The engineering insight was brutal in its elegance: the wall doesn't need to break if the person behind it does. SSDC-4 units are calibrated with an onboard micro-processor that reads surface material density and adjusts detonation profile to maintain resonance coupling across concrete, composite alloy, and reinforced polymer.

Operators call it 'The White Flash' because survivors — those at the edge of the effective radius — report a blinding white visual event with no accompanying sound, followed by hours of confusion and vomiting. Those at the center of the cone are found in what breach teams describe as 'the quiet position': seated, slumped, or standing still, with no visible wounds and no capacity for coherent response.
specifications:
form factor: Flat adhesive charge panel, 200mm x 140mm x 18mm
weight: 420g including adhesive backing
detonation mode: Remote trigger, timer, or contact proximity
effective cone: 2.0m radius, 90-degree arc behind surface
surface penetration: Effective through up to 280mm reinforced concrete equivalent
calibration time: 1.1 seconds automatic surface density scan
primary effect: Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, acute intracranial pressure spike
secondary effects: Persistent confusion, photophobia, loss of fine motor control in survivors at range
tactical_use: Breach teams affix the SSDC-4 to walls, floors, or vehicle hulls before entry, detonating it to incapacitate occupants without alerting building structural sensors or creating entry points that invite counterfire. It is also used in hostage situations to neutralize a room's armed occupants while leaving the structural geometry intact for immediate entry. Some operators use pairs of charges on opposing walls to create overlapping cones that cover an entire room.
cultural_context: The SSDC-4 occupies a strange legal grey zone in GLMZ — its classification as 'restricted' rather than prohibited stems from successful lobbying by TESSERA CORPONATION framing it as a hostage rescue tool. Civil liberties organizations have spent years documenting its use in labor dispute suppression and protest clearance, where the lack of visible structural damage lets operators claim no explosive device was used. Among breach specialists, owning a calibrated SSDC-4 is a professional credential — a sign you work operations too sensitive for conventional entry.
known_users: TESSERA CORPONATION internal security rapid response
Black market resellers supplying organized crime for vault operations
story_hooks: A journalist investigating labor suppression has evidence an SSDC-4 was used on a union meeting hall — but TESSERA's records show all units are accounted for.
A player character wakes up in a cleared room with no memory of the last six hours — someone used an SSDC-4 on a building they were in.
A calibration error in a recent production batch is causing SSDC-4s to overpenetrate — they're killing instead of incapacitating, and TESSERA is quietly recalling units before anyone notices.
A fence is selling SSDC-4s with the corporate calibration chips still active — meaning TESSERA can track every detonation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flat, rectangular adhesive charge panel with a clinical, almost medical aesthetic — like a high-tech patch or smart bandage. The surface is dominated by a central circular piezoelectric array surrounded by concentric rings of microcircuitry. Despite its lethal function, it has an almost inert, unassuming appearance until you notice the precision engineering.
physical_description.dimensions: 200mm width × 140mm height × 18mm depth. Compact enough to palm, substantial enough to feel engineered.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light — 420g total — which creates cognitive dissonance with its destructive capability. Feels balanced, with weight distributed evenly across the panel. The adhesive backing adds negligible mass but increases tactile grip friction.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite body with embedded piezoelectric ceramic discs. Backing is industrial-grade pressure-sensitive adhesive on synthetic polymer substrate.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with a subtle iridescent sheen across the piezoelectric array — optical interference from the crystalline structure. The surface is micro-textured to prevent fingerprints and reflect minimal light. Minimal gloss; maximum stealth.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte gray-black. Accents: faint iridescent blue-violet from the piezoelectric crystals under certain angles. Minimal branding in dull silver.
physical_description.grip_texture: The adhesive backing is tacky but not sticky; designed to conform to irregular surfaces without premature adhesion. The exposed top surface is micro-ridged for stability during placement.
distinctive_features: Central honeycomb pattern of piezoelectric ceramic discs arranged in a 70mm diameter circle
Three micro-LED status indicators (power, calibration, armed) embedded flush into the upper right corner
Recessed circular detonation port (8mm diameter) at the geometric center, barely visible
Hairline engraved calibration reference grid (0-280mm scale) along the bottom edge
Moisture-resistant gasket seal running the perimeter — thin line of translucent silicone
Serial number and manufacturer stamp (Lucid Dreams Sleep Technology logo) in 4pt font, bottom left corner
Thermochromic ink that reveals internal circuit topology when temperature exceeds 25°C (debugging feature retained from development)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Lucid Dreams Sleep Technology logo — a minimalist sleeping eye icon — stamped in matte silver at bottom left. Serial number in 4pt numerals directly below. No other markings; the aesthetic is deliberately corporate-clinical, suggesting medical/therapeutic origin rather than military.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breach operators keep these in pristine condition until deployment. After adhesive application to a surface, the visible face remains clean and unmarred — the weapon is invisible until detonation. Pre-deployment units show no wear; post-mission units are considered single-use and disposed of.

Shot with surgical precision lighting — cool 5600K key light from upper left, deep shadow fill on the right side creating dimensional contrast. Background is pure black with slight vignette. No hands, no scale reference — let the engineering speak. Hyper-detailed macro focus on the surface texture and crystal structure.
